clue.text: Act getting equipment to turn corner

parts.note: to act is to do something, so this gives DO
gear is kit or equipment

explanation.surface: An actor acquires some props in order to round a bend on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is only a link joining the two pieces. The definition is a verb: to fold down the corner of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog-ear a book is to fold down the corner of one of its pages.

clue.text: Emits gas skyward, securing incomplete image of sports icon

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a clasp secures what it grips
in a down clue going skyward means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: farts is a coarse word for emits gas

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, leaving it unfinished

parts.note: an effigy is an image or likeness of a person

explanation.surface: Someone breaks wind upward while holding a partial portrait of a sporting hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The incomplete image is EFFIGY missing its last letter. Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf, the German tennis champion of many Grand Slams, is a celebrated figure of the sport.

clue.text: Like Dad's mate embracing a bird

indicators.note: the outer word wraps its arms round the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a pal is a mate or friend
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A father's friend gives a bird a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternal means relating to or characteristic of a father, hence like Dad's.

clue.text: Bound once more to precede senior clergywoman (some day?)

indicators.note: the piece for once more comes before the piece for bound in the answer

parts.note: bis is a musical instruction meaning repeat, or twice
to bound is to hop or leap

explanation.surface: A woman leaps again on her way to becoming a senior churchwoman one day.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is from Latin, used in music for 'again'. The question mark admits that women bishops were still in the future when the puzzle was set.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy; the clue looks ahead to women holding that office.

clue.text: Slightly sweaty man put back inside and executed

indicators.note: one piece goes within the letters of another

parts.note: beaded with sweat, glistening with small drops

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round, read from its end

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A clammy fellow is sent back in and put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly sweaty' means covered in small beads of sweat; the reversed man sits just after the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead someone is to execute them by cutting off the head.

clue.text: Want inshore label?

indicators.note: the first two letters of inshore act as a separate word, telling us the label goes into the shore

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about lacking a coastal sticker.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'inshore' as two words, 'in shore': the label goes in the coast. 'Want' is a noun here, meaning lack, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or scarcity is a shortage.

clue.text: Turning tail, Stan discovers lost city

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Stan turns tail and stumbles on a legendary vanished city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like part of the phrase 'turning tail', but it is the anagram signal working on TAIL and STAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island city said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Thank you — thank you and goodbye!

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
again ta, informal thanks

explanation.surface: An effusive farewell that keeps saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a casual British farewell, like bye-bye.

clue.text: Fusses about with soft drink

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: ados are fusses, bustle or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss over their fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ADOS round; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink, a carbonated mixer.

clue.text: Float around nothing in vacuum

indicators.note: one piece sits around another, enclosing it

parts.note: to hover is to float in the air
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something drifts weightlessly in empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuum' is a verb or noun for the cleaner; Hoover is the brand name used generically in Britain for a vacuum cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoover is a vacuum cleaner, and to hoover is to vacuum, from the brand name.

clue.text: Put on (performed), holding back euphemism

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it

parts.note: acted means performed on stage

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: eff is a euphemism for a well-known swear word, as in effing and blinding

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a show but holds back from swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' is the definition, meaning feigned; 'eff' stands in for a swear word, as in 'effing and blinding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Put on in the sense of feigned or pretended matches a manner that is assumed, not natural.

clue.text: Cent in change causes dispute

indicators.note: one letter goes into the middle of a word

parts.note: an alteration is a change

explanation.surface: Inserting a cent into the change leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or dispute.

clue.text: Block keeping drunken sot on US city's side

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next
the outer word keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: an anvil is the iron block a blacksmith works on

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger into another order

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, a US city; the 's adds no letters

explanation.surface: A drinker is barred from a team belonging to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' shakes up 'sot', and the result sits just after the first letter of the block. Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club; 'side' means team.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English football club, and a side is a team.

clue.text: Do away with troubled rest in pipe

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or channel

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Destroy something whose rest in a pipe has been disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do away with' is the definition, as a verb; 'troubled' rearranges 'rest', which sits after the pipe's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To destruct is to destroy deliberately, to do away with something.

clue.text: Following rules, doctor's kept boiling hot

indicators.note: the outer word keeps the other piece within it

parts.note: a medic is a doctor; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: boiling suggests the letters bubble into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor kept something scalding hot, as the rules required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor's' reads as 'doctor has'; 'boiling' scrambles 'hot', which the doctor keeps inside after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodic means systematic, working by a set procedure.

clue.text: Stick in broken fragment, having lost first bit of mosaic

indicators.note: broken suggests the word is smashed and its letters reassembled
the word loses a letter, which is then gone
first bit means the opening letter only

explanation.surface: A piece of a mosaic, broken and missing a tile, is stuck back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' takes the M ('first bit of mosaic') from FRAGMENT, and 'broken' rearranges the remaining FRAGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To engraft is to graft one thing into another, to fix or implant it.

clue.text: Recondite, strong, offensive language put about

indicators.note: the outer word is placed round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: abuse is insulting or offensive language

explanation.surface: Obscure, forceful swearing gets spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong' looks like a description of the language, but it is a separate piece, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse means hard to understand, obscure, much as recondite does.

clue.text: Take weight off king, priest and first lady

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel
Eve, in the Bible, was the first woman

explanation.surface: A royal, a cleric and a president's wife lighten someone's load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife but means the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to ease a burden, literally or figuratively lightening a load.

clue.text: Hence no wonderful hankering for far from wonderful person

parts.note: so means therefore, hence
fab is informal for fabulous, wonderful
an itch is a craving or hankering

explanation.surface: A long yearning for something not so great after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link. 'wonderful' is wordplay the first time and part of the definition the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a vulgar insult for a contemptible, unpleasant person.

clue.text: Intermediary's more skint?

definitions.meaning: a go-between who arranges deals for others; the 's stands for is
skint is British slang for penniless, so more broke

explanation.surface: Is a middleman poorer than others?
explanation.definitionFit: A broker negotiates between buyer and seller; and someone with less money than another is more hard up.

clue.text: Super-10

definitions.meaning: ...- as a prefix means chief or supreme, as in archenemy
points to the answer at 10 across, meaning mannered or put on

explanation.definitionFit: Arch means chief or principal, and also playfully knowing or mannered in behaviour.

clue.text: Junky delivering final bits of The Walrus and the Carpenter

indicators.note: the closing pair of letters is taken from each of the two named words

explanation.surface: An addict recites the end of Lewis Carroll's poem about two beachcombers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final bits' here means the last two letters of each: walrUS and carpentER. The Walrus and the Carpenter is a poem in Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A junky is a drug addict, someone who takes drugs regularly.

clue.text: Hold back when others pour

parts.note: the rest means the others, those remaining
to rain is to pour down

explanation.surface: Keep yourself in check while everyone else is pouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep under control.

clue.text: Interrupted by apex of triangle — spherical, or getting on that way?

definitions.text: spherical, or getting on that way?

indicators.note: a letter breaks into the middle of a word

parts.note: round means spherical, ball-shaped

indicators.note: the apex is the top, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: a triangle's tip breaks into a sphere, or is it a body growing plumper?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spherical' does double duty, giving ROUND and starting the definition; the rest hints at someone getting rounder, plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means round in shape, and also plump or portly, which a body becomes over time.

clue.text: Marketing method making unhaloed heads roll

indicators.note: making heads roll suggests the letters tumble about into a new arrangement
a halo is a ring, the shape of the letter O, so this removes an O

explanation.surface: A sales technique that gets people sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhaloed' strips the O from ROLL, and 'making' rearranges HEADS plus RLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard sell is aggressive, high-pressure selling, a technique in marketing.

clue.text: Empty cesspit into such a tank?

indicators.note: into suggests the remaining letters are poured into a new form, made into something else
emptying the pit drains away part of its contents, here one of its two S letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for draining a sewage pit into a suitable tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' drops one S from CESSPIT, and 'into' signals that CESPIT is reshaped. The blogger thought emptying a weak way to remove a single letter. A septic tank is where household sewage settles.
explanation.definitionFit: A septic tank holds sewage, so the clue's tank of that kind is septic.
